issue.body:
Campaign: kalaluthien/campaign-base#1
Repository: kalaluthien/campaign-base

An executor that has just merged a sub-issue carries that sub-issue's whole transcript, and every turn of the next sub-issue re-reads it. `/compact` is the one thing that shrinks it, and nothing sends it. Two owner corrections on 2026-09-05 shaped what lands: compaction must fire the instant the executor is done, while that context is still in the prompt cache — run later it re-reads the whole transcript uncached and costs more than it saves; and the first draft's planner-side protocol and claim-ordering rule were too complex. One mechanism, at one moment.

Second: `AGENTS.md` states two channels in two sections with no criterion between them — § Delegate launch says a first brief arrives by `herdr agent prompt`, § The four messages says STATUS/REPORT/BLOCKED/STAND DOWN travel between sessions. A later assignment to a reused executor, the answer to a BLOCKED, and a slash command are undefined. That criterion belongs with this handoff, because both halves are the one handoff.

## What lands

1. **`campaign-claim.py release` enqueues `/compact` into the releasing session's own pane**, as its last act: `HERDR_ENV=1 herdr agent prompt <own pane> "/compact"`. herdr queues a prompt against a working pane, so compaction fires the moment the release turn ends, on the context that turn just used. The script finds its own pane by joining its harness session id to `herdr agent list`, and prints what it read — session id, pane, the command sent. **When no row names this session it says so and releases anyway**: compaction is a cost rule, not a gate, and a missing row must be visible, never silent. It never prompts a pane that is not its own.
2. **`scripts/campaign-assign.py <pane> <sub-issue>` is the planner's only assignment path.** It checks the pane is idle and has compacted since its last release — reading the pane text for the compaction marker, could-not-look printed and never silent — then sends the one-sentence prompt naming the sub-issue.
3. **The channel rule, stated once**, as one paragraph in `AGENTS.md` § The four messages naming that script: *an instruction to a session is a prompt into its pane; information between sessions is one of the four messages.* So every assignment (first or later), the answer to a BLOCKED, and `/compact` are prompts; REPORT, BLOCKED, STATUS and STAND DOWN stay messages. A prompt is the session's own user turn — hooks apply, no relay caveat; a message i
issue.title: Handing an executor its next sub-issue: compact its pane first, by a script the planner runs

B: the worker holding the claim merges on the planner's prompt, and planner.md step 9 says so.
Then stop for the planner's `DECISION` before any code.

- A session reading a large file is steered to a grep and a bounded range by something it must consume, not a third copy of the prose.
- A review subagent's diff read is exempt.

- A case for each outcome fails first, then passes: steered, exempt, small file.
- The prose copies point at the check, or go.
issue.intent:
- rule-check#429 measured reads at 35.5% of tool-result bytes (rule-check#412). Its option C, grep first and then a bounded range, served:
  - 7 of 7 runs at 9.1% of the bytes (experiment 4, issuecomment-5660485351);
  - 6 of 6 anchored runs at 2.3% (experiment 5, issuecomment-5660796247).
- Review reads scored lower, but every miss lay outside the text read, so a whole read would have missed them too.
- The owner, 2026-09-14: make C the rule for a session's reads, and keep review diffs read whole.
- The rule exists in prose already: `AGENTS.md` § Execution mode says "Read only the part of a file you need", and `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` says so too. The bytes show it is not followed, so the prose alone does not hold.
plan_items: First a `NOTE` with options, each tied to the #429 numbers and judged by bytes saved and wrong answers risked:
a `PreToolUse` hook on `Read` with no range over N lines;
a line in the brief hook;
a `filing`-shaped rule in `~/.claude/`;
others.

issue.body:
Campaign: kalaluthien/agent-workspace#1

A second session that arrives in the container root with a request that is a subtask of an open campaign — while another session on this machine already holds that campaign — is today told to "join" it, which makes it a second campaign session: it surveys, files, claims, launches, and may sync or close the anchor. Witnessed 2026-08-28: session `agent-workspace-51` filed and claimed #36 while `agent-workspace-3a` (the session running campaign #1) sat idle and learned nothing, because nothing in `AGENTS.md`, `opening-campaign`, or the protocol says a session can be an *executor*. The holding session can see the peer in `ListAgents` (liveness) but cannot tell which subtask it works or address it for STATUS, so its close gate and its retirement sweep are blind to it — the "several sessions × the protocol" gap named in #36.

The rule to add, and where it lands:

1. **AGENTS.md § Who is a campaign session.** A session whose request is a subtask of an open campaign, when `ListAgents` shows a peer session on this machine, becomes that subtask's **executor session**: it files the subtask (or takes the one it was given), claims the branch, announces the claim to the holding session, and from then on is an agent in the protocol — it answers STATUS, sends REPORT and BLOCKED, stops on STAND DOWN, and never surveys, syncs, or closes the anchor. The holding session is the peer the person named; when none was named, the announcement goes to every peer session and a peer that holds no campaign covering it ignores it. The executor keeps working the subtask the way any executor may (own hands, subagent on a worktree, or a delegate); what changes is only who it reports to.
2. **The protocol gains one message**, executor → campaign, sent once at claim: `CLAIMED <branch> <ListAgents name>`. It carries only what the executor alone knows — its address — because the branch and the issue are already GitHub facts and the name of an interactive session cannot be set to the branch after launch (the `--name`-is-the-branch rule covers launched delegates only; probe whether a running session can rename itself and, if it can, make renaming to the flattened branch the first step and keep CLAIMED for the holding session's benefit). Update the four-message table in AGENTS.md § Talking to a repository agent and the protocol's header in `spec/alloy/agent.als`.
3. **Liveness for an executor session is a `ListAgents` fact**, read the same way `herdr agent

issue.body:
Campaign: kalaluthien/agent-workspace#1

`AGENTS.md` will say, once #65 lands, that **liveness has one reader**,
`scripts/campaign-session-alive`, and that the comparison must never be
hand-rolled. Nothing enforces it.

This repository's own rule, `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` § Design: *a declared contract
stays true only while a second reader enforces it, a validator or hook on the
authoring side. With the consumer as its only reader, the contract drifts exactly
like the hardcoded copy it replaced.* The four hand-rolled copies #65 removes are
what that drift looks like when it has already happened — they were four prose
copies of one test, and they were all wrong together.

Verified 2026-08-30: nothing under `spec/` or `docs/` mentions
`campaign-session-alive`; the only "one reader" sentence in `spec/` is
`ledger.als:27`, about `alloy-check`.

**The scope is wider than liveness.** Three scripts now hold rules that prose
elsewhere restates or could restate — `campaign-repos`, `campaign-settlement`,
`campaign-local-work` — and `campaign-settlement`'s header already says in words
that a second implementation of its reading would drift. So the thing to build is
one authoring-side check, not one guard per script.

The work:

1. Decide what the check reads. A candidate: a grep-based guard that fails when a
   tracked file outside `scripts/` contains a hand-rolled form of a rule a script
   owns — `ps -o comm=`/`ucomm` against a literal, a `## Repos` parse, a
   settled/closable verdict. Name the forms explicitly; a check that tries to
   recognise "a reading" in general will either miss everything or fire on prose
   that quotes the retired form on purpose, which `AGENTS.md` now does
   deliberately.
2. Decide where it runs. A `pre-commit` guard is the shape this machine already
   uses for the no-direct-commits rule.
3. State, beside each script that owns a rule, that the guard is its second

restated anywhere outside it, report that with the evidence and close this
without building a guard. What must not happen is the claim standing in
`AGENTS.md` with nothing behind it.

issue.body:
Campaign: kalaluthien/agent-workspace#1

A second session that arrives in the container root with a request that is a subtask of an open campaign — while another session on this machine already holds that campaign — is today told to "join" it, which makes it a second campaign session: it surveys, files, claims, launches, and may sync or close the anchor. Witnessed 2026-08-28: session `agent-workspace-51` filed and claimed #36 while `agent-workspace-3a` (the session running campaign #1) sat idle and learned nothing, because nothing in `AGENTS.md`, `opening-campaign`, or the protocol says a session can be an *executor*. The holding session can see the peer in `ListAgents` (liveness) but cannot tell which subtask it works or address it for STATUS, so its close gate and its retirement sweep are blind to it — the "several sessions × the protocol" gap named in #36.

The rule to add, and where it lands:

1. **AGENTS.md § Who is a campaign session.** A session whose request is a subtask of an open campaign, when `ListAgents` shows a peer session on this machine, becomes that subtask's **executor session**: it files the subtask (or takes the one it was given), claims the branch, announces the claim to the holding session, and from then on is an agent in the protocol — it answers STATUS, sends REPORT and BLOCKED, stops on STAND DOWN, and never surveys, syncs, or closes the anchor. The holding session is the peer the person named; when none was named, the announcement goes to every peer session and a peer that holds no campaign covering it ignores it. The executor keeps working the subtask the way any executor may (own hands, subagent on a worktree, or a delegate); what changes is only who it reports to.
2. **The protocol gains one message**, executor → campaign, sent once at claim: `CLAIMED <branch> <ListAgents name>`. It carries only what the executor alone knows — its address — because the branch and the issue are already GitHub facts and the name of an interactive session cannot be set to the branch after launch (the `--name`-is-the-branch rule covers launched delegates only; probe whether a running session can rename itself and, if it can, make renaming to the flattened branch the first step and keep CLAIMED for the holding session's benefit). Update the four-message table in AGENTS.md § Talking to a repository agent and the protocol's header in `spec/alloy/agent.als`.
